chapter_title: Concept of Mole and Chemical Calculation

sections.content_markdown:
A $\text{NaCl}$ molecule has $1$ $\text{Na}$ atom and $1$ $\text{Cl}$ atom. Therefore, the molecular mass of $\text{NaCl} = \text{atomic mass of Na} + \text{atomic mass of Cl} = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5$

One mole of $\text{NaCl} = 58.5 \text{ g NaCl}$

$\text{CuSO}_4\cdot5\text{H}_2\text{O}$ contains $01$ $\text{Cu}$, $01$ $\text{S}$, $09$ $\text{O}$ and $10$ $\text{H}$ atoms. Therefore, the molecular mass of $\text{CuSO}_4\cdot5\text{H}_2\text{O} = \text{atomic mass of Cu} \times 1 + \text{atomic mass of S} \times 1 + \text{atomic mass of O} \times 9 + \text{atomic mass of H} \times 10$

$$= 1 \times 63.5 + 1 \times 32 + 9 \times 16 + 10 \times 1$$

$$= 249.5$$

A mole of $\text{CuSO}_4\cdot5\text{H}_2\text{O} = 249.5 \text{ g CuSO}_4\cdot5\text{H}_2\text{O}$

**Problem:** What is the mass of $1$ $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ molecule?

**Solution:** We know, $1 \text{ mole } \text{H}_2\text{O} = 18 \text{ g } \text{H}_2\text{O} = 6.023 \times 10^{23} \text{ no of } \text{H}_2\text{O} \text{ molecule}$

Here, the molecular mass of $6.02 \times 10^{23} \text{ H}_2\text{O} \text{ molecules} = 18 \text{ g}$

Therefore, the mass of $1 \text{ H}_2\text{O} \text{ molecule} = \frac{18}{6.023 \times 10^{23}} \text{ g} = 2.99 \times 10^{-23}\text{g}$

**Problem:** How many $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ molecules are there in $1\text{g}$ $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$?

**Solution:** We know, $1 \text{ mole } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 98 \text{ g } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 6.023 \times 10^{23} \text{ no of } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \text{ molecule}$

Here, $98 \text{ g } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 6.023 \times 10^{23} \text{ no of } \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \text{ molecules}$

Therefore, the mass of $1\text{g}$ $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = \frac{6.023 \times 10^{23}}{98} = 6.14 \times 10^{21} \text{ H}_2\text{SO}_4 \text{ molecules}$.

**Problem:** Calculate the mole of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ present in $5\text{g}$ $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

**Solution:** We know, $1 \text{ mole } \text{H}_2\text{O} = 18\text{g } \text{H}_2\text{O} = 6.023 \times 10^{23} \text{ no of } \text{H}_2\text{O} \text{ molecules}$.

Here, $18 \text{ g } \text{H}_2\text{O} = 1 \text{ mole } \text{H}_2\text{O}$

$1\text{g } \text{H}_2\text{O} = \frac{1}{18} \text{ mole } \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Therefore, $5 \text{ g } \text{H}_2\text{O} = \frac{1 \times 5}{18} = 0.277 \text{ mole } \text{H}_2\text{O}$.
